name: Cyberdesk
long_description:
Cyberdesk is the first self learning computer use agent for developers to automate desktop workflows. 

For example, one of our customers is building an AI agent for hospital patient intake, and they’re using us to automate an entire team of people manually clicking and typing into a desktop app to book appointments. 

We launched mid July, and our agent is already operating in production environments, creating appointments in electronic health record apps and processing files in legacy ERPs.

We’ve built the first computer use agent that memorizes tasks and repeats them quickly while still adapting to unexpected changes on the screen. A good analogy is to how humans use computers: once we get used to an app, we use it much faster, while still adapting to random popups and crashes. This new paradigm for computer use will be needed by every company automating human workflows on computers.

Mahmoud previously built robotic process automation solutions impacting 20K+ employees at a Fortune 100 company. He also built AI & ML solutions at Baylor College of Medicine Neuroscience & Texas Children's Hospital + co-published a paper at the Rice Networks Group. 

Alan is ex-NASA and previously dropped out to be the first founding engineer at a PearX startup. He is a second time founder, having previously built and scaled a consumer AI app to thousands of paying users.

Computer-use agents will automate the $6T dollars spent on enterprise knowledge work and Cyberdesk will be the platform to power this.

We’d love to talk with you!
https://cal.com/mahmoud-al-madi-klrs5s/30min
one_liner: Self learning computer use agent for developers

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer:
We met 2 years ago, connecting over our shared experiences at Rice, and our love of building things. We both ended up living at the same Hacker House in Menlo Park, called Incepto! We started Cyberdesk with the realization that it’s really hard to build a great computer use agent, especially when it comes to reliability, speed, and cost. We both lived in a 9×9 Airbnb room with a tiny bed and a single desk (we call it the Cyberdesk lol) and got Cyberdesk off the ground, building the MVP in a 6 days and getting a paid customer the next day through a cold email. \
\
Cyberdesk was built to solve all three of the core problems with off the shelf computer use models: speed, reliability, and cost. We’re excited to deploy this architecture to the world and become the best developer framework for computer use.

question_answers.question: How did you decide to apply to Y Combinator? What was your experience applying, going through the batch, and fundraising at demo day?
question_answers.answer: From the moment we started working together, we knew we wanted to go through YC together. It was a little over a month before the deadline for Summer 2025 came out when we started working together, so we got to work! We launched, got paid customers, and built out our infrastructure fast. A month later, we interviewed in person and got the call from Jon Xu the same night that we got in! It was one of the happiest days of our lives.

question_answers.question: What's the history of your company from getting started until the present day? What were the big inflection points?
question_answers.answer:
We started working together in late March (2025), with a shared goal of solving deep developer problems around computer use. We started off with an idea to help developers spin up virtual desktops for computer use agents in a single line of code. We shipped an MVP in 5 days and got a paid customer the next day through a cold email. For the next month, we kept shipping and looking for customers, and applied to YC with this idea. We found the product had interest from hobbyist developers, but for companies, there was much less pull because companies often already have VM infrastructure they are happy with. \
\
So we made the call to pivot. We talked to over 100 developers in the computer use and robotic process automation space, and heard the same thing over and over: automating Windows desktops is an important yet extremely tedious process. You create a script once, then it breaks every time something changes in the app or a popup happens. Computer use agents were meant to solve that pain but even they were slow, costly, and non deterministic. That’s how we came up with the idea for what Cyberdesk is today - a layer on top of computer use agents that helps it memorize tasks it’s done before and repeat it consistently, 3 - 5x faster, and cheaply, while still falling back to computer use during popups and anomalies. We built an MVP in a week, and got our first pilot a week later. \
\
Since then we’ve been rapidly building out the product and closing more deals with startups and companies in healthcare, construction, accounting, and more, all of them using our agent to automate manual computer work they’ve struggled to automate before.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
For a developer team to automate legacy desktop apps with poor APIs, they’ve often resorted to building brittle automation scripts (either in Python or using a legacy RPA tool like UiPath) or hiring unreliable remote workers to click on remote desktops. As they need to support more and more software and versions of that software, the development and maintenance times exponentially increases. \
\
Every company in the world has repetitive manual desktop work that is bogging them down. On top of that, companies building AI agents are increasingly having to interface with desktop apps to perform full human workflows. This problem is pervasive and we’re excited to solve it.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer: Traditional robotic process automation is a $6 billion industry, yet it only services a tiny fraction of desktop tasks that can now be automated by our agent. In the long term, our agent will automate every manual computer task.

launches.tagline: Automate legacy apps like EHRs, ERPs, and more with just a prompt and an API call to our agent
launches.body:
Hey everyone! We’re Mahmoud and Alan, co-founders of Cyberdesk.

**🏆 TL;DR:**

We’re building a computer use agent for developers to automate legacy Windows apps like EHRs, ERPs, and more. Just write your task in plain English, and call our API to trigger our agent. Our agent is designed to follow memorized steps reliably, only falling back to computer use models during expected popups.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yCDGsiCNb3E

**❌ The Problem**

Developers in industries like healthcare, supply chain, and beyond often work with clients who have old, legacy Windows software. Today, to work with these clients, they probably:

* Hire unreliable offshore teams to manually click through remote desktops
* Write fragile automation scripts that break on popups and need constant fixes
* Skip the integration entirely—leaving valuable customers behind

**✨ Our Solution**

Just write your task in plain English, and our computer use agent will run it reliably, cheap, and fast, on any Windows PC (cloud or on prem).

Example: entering patient data into OpenDental, a legacy dental EHR (real use case from one of our customers)

1. **Write the task** (”Log in to Opendental, click Patients, find this dropdown, etc”), then just call our API to trigger the workflow
2. **Our agent learns the task.** Every time it repeats the task, it does it 100% deterministically, upwards of 3x faster, and almost zero cost
3. **If something unexpected happens** (like a popup), our system falls back to the computer use agent, and memorizes that trajectory too

Mahmoud (CEO) previously scaled robotic process automation solutions to 20k employees at a Fortune 100. Alan (CTO) is ex-NASA and built a computer use agent at his previous startup.

launches.body:
**TL;DR: [Pangolin](https://digpangolin.com) is an [open-source](https://github.com/fosrl/pangolin) cloud and self-hostable alternative to Cloudflare Tunnels, Zscaler ZPA, and Ngrok. Pangolin provides a simple way to securely expose applications on private networks with identity-aware access control and high availability.**

We’ve seen incredible early traction since we launched 5 months ago: **12,600+ GitHub stars, 140,000+ installs, 2,700+ Discord members**. 

https://youtu.be/0nv91PgCm9M

"Pangolin isn't just a fantastically easy-to-configure VPN and reverse proxy; it's a revelation in self-hosting simplicity." XDA Developers

**The problem:**

Providing users with secure access to internal tools and infrastructure is cumbersome for both end users and administrators. They're forced to manage complex VPN clients, servers, and network configurations that create friction and operational overhead. Traditional and mesh VPN approaches require layered ACL management to control which users can access specific resources, turning simple access requests into complex network engineering problems.

**Our solution:**

Drop in the Pangolin connector in your network, and:

* **Expose anything to the internet:** Instantly create a secure tunnel with your domain and SSL to internal dashboards like Grafana, or any other services on your private network and access via web browsers.

launches.body:
Hey everyone we’re Harsha and Dhruv from Slashy. Our goal is to define the next generation of email, by building an email platform that actually works for you, and learns over time. \
\
**TLDR:** Slashy is the next big email platform after Superhuman, the first with an assistant built in. Slashy can do everything from writing drafts in your tone, texting you when an important email comes in, prepping you for calls, to the things you expect from a true email client like keyboard shortcuts, open tracking, a mobile app and more. All while continuously learning about you and your preferences, so it only gets better over time. The average user takes 5 minutes to get set up and saves an extra hour a day. Read an independent review from Tom’s guide (1m+ subscribers) [here](https://www.tomsguide.com/ai/slashy-is-the-ai-email-app-replacing-notion-mail-heres-why).

You can get started for free at [slashy.com](http://slashy.com), and use our YC deal for a long-term discount.

**Launch Video:** <https://youtu.be/o2TN-wwCYm8>

## **Problem**

Most founders we speak to, have one of two problems (sometimes both)

1. They spend too much time manually handling email, and not enough building their company.
2. They don’t spend enough time on email, and lose important deals/hires due to things slipping.

## **Solution**

That’s why we built Slashy, the first email platform that reliably gets work done for you, whether it be drafting emails, notifying you when a prospect replies, schedule meetings, or more. Slashy works wherever you work best, so onboarding is seamless (just ask some of our users). It takes 10 minutes to set up, and saves the average email power user an extra one hour a day. It does this by:

1. **Doing all the basic things right:** Stuff like keyboard shortcuts, open tracking, unified inbox, team comments, availability links, all come part of Slashy. So you don’t lose anything transitioning from Gmail, Superhuman, Front and more. ([@Jayme Hoffman](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/60463) actually switched to Slashy being surprised just that a new email client could match the speed, shortcuts of something like Superhuman)
2. **Writing drafts that sound like you:** Claude drafts sound like slop because they just look at the thread. Slashy does a lot more, it looks at the linkedin/web of recipients, past emails you’ve sent, past changes you’ve made to prior drafts, and more including using our own custom-built memory system for email. (Fun fact we have a special tool for handling suggesting times/scheduling as base llms are very bad at this). ([@Michelle Marcelline](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/379052) pretty much just hits send on all her Slashy drafts with minimal edits)
3. **A powerful sidebar:** Slashy comes with a cursor-like sidebar. That lets you do things like search, draft, schedule and more. So you no longer need to keep flipping between ChatGPT and your email. ([@Yahia Bakour](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2538368) loves this to power thorugh drafts and replies)
4. **Integrations:** Slashy connects to not just your email, but your meeting notes (Granola, Fathom, Circleback, etc.), crm (Attio, Hubspot, Salesforce, etc.), Notion and more since the context to handle email isn’t just in email. ([@Pavlos Markesinis](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2511438) loves how Slashy connects to his Attio and makes life simple)
5. **Automations:** The best assistants also know when to handle things in the background. So Slashy can also automatically do things like prep you for calls, text you when an important email comes in, and more. ([@Owen Botkin](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2579867) relies on Slashy to prep him from calls, and [@Pranav Madhukar](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1531197) doesn’t even check his email anymore unless Slashy alerts him an email comes in)
6. **iMessage/Slack Bot:** One of the worst parts of traditional clients? You need to open them to see if something important comes in. Slashy can ping you on text/slack so you don’t even need to context switch. (@devansh is one of our bigger Slack fans, while [@Abhinav Gopal](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/979064) for iMessage).
7. **Voice:** Sometimes it’s easier to speak your mind than write (or you’re driving and just can’t haha). So Slashy lets you dictate your thoughts, and our AI will make it sound like a much better version of you. Or you can talk with our voice to voice agent when you’re commuting (@vishruth is one of our power users for our voice drafts).
8. **Personalized Memory:** Slashy gets better the more you use it. It keeps notes on how you write, who you talk to, when you schedule, and also it learns from every edit you made before hitting send. It even once a week goes back and rewrites its notes to better match you. After all you'd expect a human assistant to be smarter after a few months, why not your ai one. ([@Devraj Gopal](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2057015) loves how Slashy has grown to know him more and more).
9. **Natural Language Labels:** A common complaint we hear is the rise of the AI SDR, and how everyone’s inbox is inundated with emails. The problem with traditional labelling systems is they don’t adjust over time, leading to important emails getting missed. Slashy’s labelling system does, leading to a much better filtering rate, and fewer dropped balls. ([@Nazli Danis](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/520906) was drowning in spam before Slashy)

## Security and Privacy

We take security/privacy as an email client very seriously.  We’ve already gotten CASA, and SOC II. We also get monthly pen-tests done by [@Casco](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/30477) to ensure our users' data is safe. None of our AI providers train on your data as well.

## Getting Started

Now if you want to get started just go to[ slashy.com](http://slashy.com), or you can book a time here if you’d like me to demo the product/ask any questions just shoot an email to [founders+ea@slashy.com](mailto:founders+ea@slashy.com), and Slashy will schedule a time that works for both of us :)

Hey everyone 👋

We’re [Tim](https://www.linkedin.com/in/timcherkasov/) and [Artur](https://www.linkedin.com/in/artur-romanov/) – co-founders of [Trace](https://www.trace.so/).

**📙 TL;DR**

Trace is a workflow automation platform that routes tasks to the right agent – human or AI.

By connecting to tools like Slack, Jira, and Notion, Trace breaks down existing workflows, spots automation opportunities, and embeds AI agents to handle repetitive tasks – without disrupting how your team works. More than 30 companies already use Trace to automate gruntwork.

**Ask**: If you’re currently working in operations, product, or support teams, we’d love to talk. Email us at [founders@trace.so](mailto:founders@trace.so) ‼️

https://youtu.be/RfJerH9r2-8

**❌ The Problem**

Most teams lose ≈ 40% of their productivity on repetitive manual tasks. 

Routine work like chasing updates, filling docs, coordinating teams, and handling support drains hours, breaks focus, and slows execution.

Meanwhile, employees aren’t sure which tasks can be automated, which agents to use, or which tools to trust – problems made worse by fragmented data and lost context.

Even worse, most AI tools work alone, disconnected from both teams and the people using them.

✅ **Our Solution** 

Trace is an AI-native workspace that breaks down existing workflows, assigns repetitive tasks to AI agents, and routes the rest to the right people.

With Trace, AI works across your entire team – passing tasks between agents and people without disrupting operations.

It respects permissions, learns from past and ongoing work, tracks progress with a full audit trail, and lets you review, edit, or reroute tasks in a simple interface.

**Connect and Prompt Away**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=92892&key=user_uploads/1016719/794551f2-0e27-4ccf-a406-326622b90d15)

How? – Through a company wide context engine!

By integrating with your systems, our context engine analyzes your internal wiki, activity logs, and people data to understand your team’s work.

Trace then builds a unified index of your company and provides rich context for every new workflow, making it easy to route tasks between people and AI agents.

launches.body:
Coding tools have 10x’d not only dev speed, but also the surface area for bugs. The bottleneck has shifted to validating that features and fixes _actually_ work. 

Your team is probably spending hours doing at least one of these things:

* Manually testing for regressions
* Writing and maintaining brittle E2E test scripts
* Saying “f\*ck it, ship it,” way too often

All while still having users complain about bugs that slip into prod…

“Can’t my coding agent just write my E2E tests for me?”

Sure - but now you’re stuck maintaining them as your app evolves - broken selectors, missing element IDs, new user journeys, non-deterministic environments, evolving infra requirements…

Not to mention the cases that are nearly impossible to test with scripts in the first place: Apple Pay, in-app browser flows, complex swipes, drag-and-drop, magic links, OAuth, cross-app auth, etc…

This is why we built **Autosana** - **the agentic E2E testing layer to close the loop with your coding agents.** Fully vision based, testing your app like humans would. 

* Get onboarded seamlessly via our [MCP](https://docs.autosana.ai/mcp-setup)
* Runs locally and in our cloud for multi-env testing
* Code review + E2E testing in your PR with video proof
* Tests evolving with your codebase, creating & running tests based on PR context and code diffs
* Works across iOS, Android, mobile web, and desktop web

Hey guys!

We’re Uv and Jason from Autosana 🌊

We’re building a QA agent that tests mobile apps like a real user. We’re on a mission to make flaky selector-based test scripts (or worse, manual regression testing) things of the past.

[Demo here :)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zsY22nvcVLU)

# **TL;DR**

* Cloud-hosted mobile QA agent (iOS and Android)
* Natural language → simulated user flows
* Integrates into CI/CD
* Saves 8+ eng. hours per deployment

# **Problem**

**Dev Tools Have Evolved — QA Tools Haven’t**

Tools like Cursor and Claude Code boost dev speed by 10x, but lack the runtime context to write E2E tests, especially for complex and non-deterministic flows.

**The QA Bottleneck**

Maintaining traditional end-to-end scripts using frameworks like Appium, Espresso, and XCUITest wastes valuable engineering resources (trust us, we’ve been there).

These tests are tedious to write, brittle, and routinely break with UI changes. Many mobile teams ($100B+ companies included) have abandoned them and rely on manual QA.

# **Solution**

We started Autosana to fix the QA bottleneck and help mobile teams ship faster without fear of breaking things.

Just describe your test flows with natural language, as if you’re talking to your own **in-house QA Engineer**. No code, no infra setup, no dependence on flaky element selectors, and no more manual work.

Our agent tests your app like a real user, as **part of your CI/CD** pipeline or on a schedule, and **reports to the team when bugs are found**.

Autosana supports both iOS and Android, and is framework-agnostic (we support React Native, Flutter, Swift, Kotlin, you name it…).

**Mobile QA shouldn’t be hard. We’re on a mission to fix the bottleneck between mobile development and testing.**

Have a bug-free day (or many bug-free days, with Autosana <3)

# Knowlify — The AI video company for business

## 📙 TL;DR

Your team writes great docs that nobody reads. Knowlify turns those docs and ideas into narrated, animated videos — make them yourself on our platform in minutes, or have our studio produce them for you. Backed by Y Combinator and already used by teams at Amazon, ByteDance, Flexport, Supabase, and Cerebras.

👉 [knowlify.com](http://knowlify.com) · [Start free](https://create.knowlify.com) · [Book a demo](https://calendly.com/knowlify/meeting)

## Who We Are

We're Ritam, Jon, Ritvik, and Arjun — four friends who met at the University of Florida. We started Knowlify because we were tired of dense material nobody actually absorbs. We began by helping learners turn confusing content into clear explainer videos, and something kept happening: it wasn't just students who needed this. Onboarding teams, training managers, marketers, and comms leads kept asking us to turn _their_ documents into video too.

So we followed the pull. Today Knowlify is the AI video company for business.

## The Problem

Every company runs on documents — onboarding guides, SOPs, training manuals, product specs, safety procedures, internal updates. And almost nobody reads them.

* People retain far more from a short video than from a wall of text, yet most company knowledge still lives in PDFs and slide decks.
* Making real video is slow and expensive. A single explainer from an agency can cost thousands of dollars and take weeks.
* Teams need _more_ video than they could ever have time or budget to make — so most of their content never becomes video at all.

The result is a constant gap between the volume of content teams produce and the volume of video they can actually create.

## Our Solution

Knowlify closes that gap two ways:

**Knowlify Platform — you make the video.** Upload a doc, a blog post, or just an idea, and get a narrated, animated video in minutes. Editing is as simple as chatting with it. It's self-serve, fast, and built for teams that need to produce a lot of video on their own schedule. [Start free →](https://create.knowlify.com)

**Knowlify Studio — we make it for you.** When the stakes are high, our production team writes, animates, and delivers the whole thing end to end — final video in as little as 72 hours. From hyperrealistic launch films to photoreal safety training, the studio handles it. [Book a call →](https://calendly.com/knowlify/meeting)

One platform for the everyday volume, one studio for the flagship pieces. Both turn the content you already have into video people actually watch.

## Who's Using It

We work with teams across onboarding, internal comms, learning & development, training, marketing, and customer education — in industries from healthcare and finance to manufacturing, supply chain, and medtech. Teams at Amazon, ByteDance, Colliers, Flexport, Zuru, Cerebras, Supabase, Zoho, and IntSig already make video with Knowlify.

> "We worked with Knowlify to convert our written, complicated patient instructions into a short video. It helped us address an important pain-point with customers who had trouble following instructions." — David Manka, PhD, COO, PS Fertility

> "Your platform does exactly what I need — converting my papers to videos so they can be accessed and understood by more people." — Matthew Traum, PhD, University of Florida

## The Ask

If your team produces more content than it has time to turn into video — onboarding, training, comms, product, marketing — we'd love to help.

* Try it yourself: [create.knowlify.com](http://create.knowlify.com)

launches.title: Nexus – Enabling Business Teams to Build AI Agents Without Code
launches.tagline: Build agent without waiting for the engineering team
launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94339&key=user_uploads/1212509/d8f3dd70-cd99-48ee-b914-f303f372157c)

**TL;DR:** Nexus is a platform enabling non-technical business teams to create production-ready AI agents in days, not months.

---

## We're Nexus

We're Assem and Shady, the Nexus team. We've been in the AI trenches since 2019, and we kept watching the same painful pattern repeat at every enterprise.

https://youtu.be/ItX32Iqx2I8

---

# The Problem: 95% of Enterprise AI Projects Fail

**MIT reported in August 2025 that 95% of enterprise AI projects fail.** The reason? Engineering can't ship fast enough.

Consider this scenario: Your sales team needs an AI agent to qualify leads, research companies, and personalize outreach. It's a perfect use case for AI. You know exactly what you need.

But here's what actually happens:

* **Engineering has a 6-12 month backlog** – Your project gets queued behind critical infrastructure work
* **By the time they start building**, GPT-5 is out and your GPT-3.5 solution is already obsolete
* **By the time they finish**, your business needs have completely changed – that lead qualification process? Your team evolved it three times already
* **The solution is rigid** – Any change means another engineering ticket and another 3-month wait

We watched this pattern destroy brilliant AI initiatives across industries. A telecom giant had a chatbot stuck with IT for over a year. Global consultancies spent 6+ months with external developers with nothing to show. Private equity firms rebuilt the same infrastructure from scratch, over and over.

**Companies that lose on speed lose big.** While you wait, competitors are moving. Markets are shifting. Opportunities are disappearing.

The bottleneck isn't ideas, budget, or even AI capabilities. **It's implementation speed.**

---

# The Solution: Give Business Teams the Power to Build

Instead of waiting for engineering or buying rigid pre-built solutions, Nexus gives enterprises the infrastructure to build their own agents reliably – **no code required**.

### **How It Works:**

**1. Create agents with natural language**

Describe what you want in plain English. "Build a agent that screens job applications, checks LinkedIn profiles, and schedules interviews with qualified candidates." and Nexus kickstarts the building of your agent from scratch

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94339&key=user_uploads/1212509/ccf88c58-51d1-47ac-8ea3-c65df19334e6)

**2. Connect your entire company stack**

Connect any system, choose any AI model, integrate any tool. With 4,000+ plugins plus custom API support, your agents work with your entire tech stack. No vendor lock-in

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94339&key=user_uploads/1212509/32849f6b-6efa-4ca7-84ad-dbfd77f82ab7)


**3. Build complex agentic workflows**\
Visual builder with AI actions, web search, data extraction, and integration with over 4,000 business apps. No coding, just drag and drop.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94339&key=user_uploads/1212509/153019f0-f934-4928-a636-53a634f24991)

**4. The Secret Sauce: Nexus Flow**

Traditional automation forces a bad tradeoff:

* **RPA tools** – Work perfectly until your process changes (then break instantly)
* **AI workflows** – Handle some variation but hit walls with real complexity
* **Open-ended agents** – Might solve it brilliantly. Might hallucinate. You never know.

**Nexus gives you both:** Our Agentic Flow lets you decide when agents should think and adapt vs. when they need zero-hallucination reliability. Full intelligence when you need it, bulletproof accuracy when it matters.

---

# Proven at Scale: Orange Belgium

https://youtu.be/MEvaTTG9IrY

Orange Belgium needed to transform their customer onboarding. Previous scripted chatbots were a good start, but customers expected natural conversations, not predefined menus.

**A non-technical team member used Nexus to build a complete AI sales agent in one week:**

* Connected to Orange's entire product catalog and internal systems
* Deployed on WhatsApp for omnichannel customer reach
* Is relentless about closing the sales while answering concerns
* Live in production, serving thousands of customers

**The Results:**

* **$4M+ in monthly revenue** generated by this single agent
* **+50% conversion rate**
* **+10 points customer satisfaction**

_"With Nexus, we've given every prospect a knowledgeable consultant available 24/7. It's like speaking to our best-trained advisor, anytime."_ – Laurent Stevens, Digital Performance Specialist, Orange Belgium

---

---

# How We Got Here

We've been building AI systems since 2019, pre-ChatGPT. We helped enterprises implement everything from custom LLM pipelines to agentic workflows.

**The breaking point came when we saw the same infrastructure being rebuilt over and over:**

* Prompt engineering frameworks
* Evaluation pipelines
* Testing infrastructure
* Integration layers
* Deployment systems
* Monitoring and observability

Every enterprise was spending 6-12 months building the exact same foundation. Meanwhile, brilliant AI ideas died in committee meetings and engineering backlogs.

We thought: **What if we built this infrastructure once, made it enterprise-grade, and let business teams build on top of it?**

That's when we knew we had something.

---

# Our Ask

We'd love to help automate your workflows – or connect you with enterprises that need this!

**If you know someone at a large organization (200+ employees) with:**

* A challenging AI roadmap stuck in implementation
* A need to integrate reliable AI across multiple departments
* Frustration with current solutions or development speed

**We'd love to chat.** Reach out to [**assem@gpt.nexus**](mailto:assem@gpt.nexus) and we can set up time to discuss how Nexus could help, or book directly at https://calendly.com/assem-obpv/nexus-demo-call

---

_P.S. – We're SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, and GDPR certified. Enterprise-grade security is built in from day one._ 🚀

launches.title: Openroll: The AI that Shows Exactly What Your Competitors Pay
launches.tagline: AI agents that reveal competitor pay and guide every salary decision.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Companies spend trillions each year on salaries but still guess what to pay. Openroll ends that. Our AI agents reveal exactly how competitors pay – company by company, role by role – and guide leaders through salary decisions in real time.

Early customers are already closing candidates they used to lose, retaining their best people, and seeing 3X ROI in week one and six-figure P&L impact.

Know any tech People/HR leaders, CFOs, or CEOs? Let’s connect: [mattias@openroll.com](mailto:mattias@openroll.com)

https://youtu.be/WfrVYtrUWmM

**Problem**

Imagine playing chess without seeing the board.

That’s how companies set pay today. Salaries decide who joins, who stays, and who leaves – yet leaders still move blindly.

In fast-moving markets, the stakes are extreme. Miss the mark and:

• The candidate you need takes a competing offer.

• A top performer walks when they discover they’re underpaid.

• Replacements cost months of time and resources.

Despite salaries being the largest spend in business, companies still rely on industry averages, gut feeling, and overpriced consultants. By the time they get an answer, it’s already too late.

The consequences of guessing on pay are brutal: lost candidates, frustrated teams, and six-figure mistakes. And even the biggest, most sophisticated companies still make them.

**What We’ve Built**

Openroll is an agentic AI platform that brings real transparency into compensation for the first time:

* **See competitor pay, company by company:** Know exactly what your peers pay their employees. No averages. No black boxes. Just transparent data.
* **AI-guided pay decisions:** From setting starting salaries to balancing cash vs. equity, agents guide leaders through the toughest calls.
* **Speed is survival:** Weeks of manual work and spreadsheets collapse into seconds – giving you the edge to win and keep the people who matter most.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94293&key=user_uploads/1762740/cabffc7c-4a3c-4956-be6d-db93d501d7b4)

**Why This Matters**

Here’s what our users say:

“Candidates we used to lose now close in days.”

“We finally know where we stand in the market.”

“Comp decisions that dragged on for weeks now take minutes.”

“For once I know what my competitors actually pay”

**Employees** love Openroll because they know pay is fair and transparent. **Managers** love it because they can act instantly and with confidence instead of wrestling with spreadsheets and guesswork. **Executives** love it because it keeps their teams together and turns compensation into a driver of growth, not risk.

The pull from tech companies has been great but any organization competing for talent is starting to see Openroll as essential infrastructure.

**Who We Are**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94293&key=user_uploads/1762740/3c74d2d1-d720-4719-953e-8d0b235a3d29)

We are **Mattias Lindell** and **Porsev Aslan**. Over the past year, we’ve lived inside the world of compensation – shadowing HR teams, interviewing leaders, and building alongside early adopters.

We’ve sat in the rooms where offers were lost and talent walked away, and we’ve refined Openroll hand-in-hand with the companies fighting to keep their people.

**Our Ask**

Know any CHROs, Heads of People, CFOs, or CEOs who care about retaining top talent? Please connect us.

Have you ever been frustrated by surveys, consultants, or guessing games around pay? We’d love to hear your stories.

Reach out at: [mattias@openroll.com](mailto:mattias@openroll.com)

We work with data-center and AI-infrastructure power, motor drives, industrial automation and robotics, industrial power supplies and conversion, battery systems and e-mobility powertrains, EV charging, solar, energy storage, grid power, HVAC, heat pumps, and appliances.

V1 boards built from off-the-shelf parts are great for getting to market quickly, but scaling to v2+ volume requires optimizing cost, size, and manufacturability. Visibl folds those parts into custom silicon built around the product: a simpler BOM, reclaimed board space, fewer supply constraints, and automation-ready assembly.

We manage the full path from architecture and design through verification, fabrication, packaging, and production-ready silicon, working alongside hardware teams so they do not need an in-house chip team.

launches.title: Visibl Semiconductors: The First AI-Enabled Coordination Layer for Chip Design
launches.tagline: Meet Visibl, The First AI-enabled Coordination Layer for Chip Design
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋\
We’re Bryce and Jordon, co-founders of VISIBL SEMICONDUCTORS™\
\
**Launch video:** <https://youtu.be/l_0BcKIIU3Q>

---

**TL;DR**\
_Visibl is the first coordination layer for chip design._ Requirements, architectural intent, and implementation drift out of sync as designs and teams scale. Visibl surfaces drift early, opens cases with evidence, and delivers review-ready fixes enabling improved schedule, cost, and risk outcomes in chip design.

Check out LinkedIn post here:\
<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/y-combinator_visibl-semiconductors-yc-w26-is-building-activity-7430280268252590081-UBoI/>

**Problem**\
Coordination has always been a human job: monitoring drift, triaging failures, keeping the schedule aligned. It demands constant vigilance, reacting to failures, proactively scanning for issues, always watching.

As designs scale, no one can hold all that context: the specs, the implementation, the test results, the decisions scattered across Slack, Jira, and docs. Issues slip through. Drift compounds. We saw this firsthand. There was no software to solve it. So we're building it.

Our experience spans chip design and high-stakes production systems. We're solving a problem there was never enough human bandwidth to address, but one that directly impacts the most important outcomes in chip design: schedule, cost, and risk.

**What Visibl Does**\
\
**Monitors** - specs, implementation, CI, and all design collateral to detect drift early

**Investigates** - creates cases with evidence: spec sections, RTL refs, CI logs, historical decisions

**Proposes** - agents suggest fixes, run verification, package review-ready diffs

**Gates** - human approval required, nothing ships without explicit sign-off

### —

\
**Results**\
\
**Schedule** - Eliminate weeks lost waiting for the one engineer with context to debug failures

**Cost** - 10x less engineering overhead on triage; your team builds instead of firefighting

**Risk** - Catch issues early to minimize rework; avoid late-stage surprises that lead to $10M+ respins\
\
\
\
\
**Instant Dispatch & Case Creation**

launches.tagline: Agents that perform IT implementations across ERPs, CRMs, and HRIS platforms.
launches.body:
Hi, we’re Assemble!

We build agents for IT teams that manage enterprise systems like ERP, CRM, and HRIS platforms. Think Salesforce, SAP, Workday, NetSuite, and custom applications. 

These **platforms keep the world’s businesses running every day**, yet they are painful to configure as the business evolves. With custom logic, integrations, and processes built up over years, IT implementations can take months or even years.

Assemble helps IT teams understand these dependencies, make changes, and test the result, all while keeping a clear agent trace. Teams can review the work, approve it, and roll it back when needed. We are building Assemble to help IT teams deliver complex transformation projects with both speed and control.

**Demo**

<https://www.loom.com/share/cf221032f60b48c9a0f0bd04dcc41041>

The demo shows Assemble migrating trade-show accounts from HubSpot to Salesforce and setting up APEX automation for hot leads. The agent completes the work end-to-end, creating an audit trail for every action letting the user revert individual changes or restore the Salesforce to an earlier snapshot.

**Why we started Assemble**

We learned about the problem space after talking to more CIOs and VPs of IT. Companies are already using AI to ask questions about their core business stack. The real challenge is to have safe-execution inside these core systems, letting IT move just as fast as the business.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105577&key=user_uploads/1578320/4aa47909-92cb-46a2-9479-917d889f318c)

Shrish (left): Cyber Security at KPMG, Mayfield Fellow. 

Aliyan (center): Researcher at Stanford AI Lab, Applied AI Engineer at Langchain, built products used by 100k+ people

Shaurnav (right): AI Engineer at Amazon and Apple. Researcher at Stanford AI Lab

We have worked on long-running agents and are excited to apply that experience to enterprise IT.

**Asks:**

1. If your company uses Salesforce, NetSuite, Workday, ServiceNow, SAP, or similar systems, we’d love to learn how your IT / business systems team handles changes today. **Are they backlogged? We might be able to help!**
2. If you know someone who leads IT, Business Systems, or Enterprise Applications at a scaling company, we’d be very grateful for an intro!

Talk to us at [founders@assemble.ai](mailto:founders@assemble.ai)

launches.title: Corelayer: AI on-call engineer for regulated industries
launches.tagline: Detect and fix production issues 15x faster
launches.body:
Hey everyone! 👋

We’re [Mitch](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mitchellradhuber/) and [Shipra](https://www.linkedin.com/in/shipra-jha-9b021859/) - before Corelayer, we built data infrastructure at Goldman Sachs where we spent many late nights and weekends debugging systems that processed 100s of billions of rows a day.

**TL;DR**

When you’re on call in data-heavy, regulated industries like fintech, healthcare, or insurance, you need to inspect underlying data to debug production issues. We built a platform that monitors both infrastructure and data for anomalies and uses AI agents to debug and suggest fixes in minutes.

[Corelayer Launch Video](https://youtu.be/yFZKJ9QRrr4)

**On-call support is painful and expensive**

All engineers hate being on call. Production issues kill velocity, erode user trust, and become more and more costly as companies scale.

Fortune 100s spend **$100M+/year** on first-line-of-defense production support.

Smaller companies can’t afford to burn **scarce engineering resources** on time-consuming support and maintenance.

**The (sensitive) data problem**

If you’re a backend engineer at a fintech, you probably own a service that queries data, applies some business logic, and stores the result somewhere (i.e., a data pipeline).

When this service is running in production, you’ll see two failure modes:

1. Exceptions in logs and/or failing jobs
2. Bad data produced by your service

“Bad data” can mean anything from incorrect values to entirely missing or duplicated rows.

**This is really common** in certain products and industries, but you’re totally blind to these errors without monitoring data for anomalies and querying data while debugging.

In regulated environments where this problem is prevalent, **production data is sensitive**, which is another constraint we have to solve for.

**Corelayer solves this**

We continuously monitor logs, metrics, **and data** for anomalies and use AI agents to debug, root-cause, and suggest fixes for issues.

Foreman is the all-in-one AI-powered project management platform built for construction contractors and the trade industry.
Today, contractors run complex businesses on a patchwork of tools that were never designed for construction — estimates in spreadsheets, plans in email, proposals copy-pasted from old Word docs, photos scattered across phones. Nothing talks to anything else, and the admin work never stops.
Foreman replaces that patchwork with a single platform that manages the full lifecycle of a construction job, from first estimate to final invoice. Contractors upload plans, photos, or a project description, and Foreman's AI instantly generates structured takeoffs, scoped estimates, and professional proposals — in minutes, not hours. From there, every customer record, document, permit, photo, change order, and conversation lives in one place, organized around the job.
The result: contractors spend less time buried in admin and more time building. They bid faster, manage jobs with less chaos, and close projects cleanly — without duct-taping five tools together to do it.

# [**🕺**](https://emojipedia.org/man-dancing)**The Team**

[**Nolan (Founder & CEO)**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nolan-rossi/) – triple majored in Electrical Engineering & Computer Science, Astrophysics, and Business Administration through UC Berkeley’s M.E.T. program, graduating in three years. He previously worked as a software development engineer at Amazon and ran a software consultancy he scaled to $250k in revenue. As a fourth-generation member of a family construction business, Nolan saw firsthand how difficult it is for contractors to consistently find new work — and how little time they have to sit down and bid on projects while managing active jobs. Scout Out was built to solve that problem.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97506&key=user_uploads/2106935/6d9cfed3-6baf-4fac-b9b7-ec2a2d99a6de)

# **❌ The Problem**

Residential contractors are running complex businesses on a patchwork of tools that were never built for construction.

* **Project management is fragmented.** Plans live in email. Estimates live in spreadsheets. Photos live on phones. Proposals get copy-pasted from old Word docs. Nothing talks to anything else.
* **Estimating is slow and error-prone.** Reading through plans, measuring takeoffs, pricing labor and materials, then assembling a professional proposal — this process takes hours and still produces mistakes. Contractors either underbid to win, or overbid to be safe, and lose anyway.
* **AI tools exist but aren't built for construction.** Generic project management software ignores the realities of field work — plan sets, per-page takeoffs, scope changes mid-build, subcontractor coordination.

  Contractors end up duct-taping tools together and paying the price in margin and stress.

**The result:** Jobs are won with incomplete bids, managed with ad-hoc systems, and closed with manual paperwork that eats hours contractors don't have.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97506&key=user_uploads/2106935/0cdecb42-5772-4e1d-81d1-1d7fb87db86d)

# **🙌 Our Solution: One Platform for the Entire Job**

Scout Out is a single platform that handles the full lifecycle of a construction job — from first estimate to final invoice — with AI doing the heavy lifting.

### Job & Customer Hub 🏗️

Everything lives in one place, organized around the job:

* Customer records and full contact history
* All uploads in one place: plans, photos, permits, contracts, and insurance
* Status tracking across every deliverable and milestone
* Every conversation, change order, and document tied to the right job

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97506&key=user_uploads/2106935/ffbb3afc-3a3e-425d-800a-23c7fc95413a)

### Instant AI-Powered Bidding ⚡

When a contractor finds a project they want, ScoutOut generates a **clean, editable quote in seconds**.

* Upload plans, photos, or a short description
* AI produces a structured estimate covering scope, labor, and materials
* Contractors can review, adjust, and send a professional bid immediately

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97506&key=user_uploads/2106935/cf8c8b3c-0744-4b8b-b092-16e0952bf102)

### Built for Real Contractor Workflows 🔧

ScoutOut is designed for how contractors actually work:

* No long setup or training
* Quotes are editable and contractor-owned
* Built to be used between site visits, calls, and active builds

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97506&key=user_uploads/2106935/f723d694-6721-4b5a-a80a-4bd39e691892)

Ritivel is an AI-native workspace for regulatory and medical writing teams at life sciences companies. Our AI agents draft CTDs, CSRs, INDs, and BLAs in minutes instead of weeks, helping drugs reach patients faster.

Every month a drug is delayed from reaching the market costs pharma companies ~$45M in lost revenue and more importantly, delays treatment for thousands of patients who need it. Yet regulatory teams are stuck in a painful, months-long process: synthesizing thousands of pages of clinical data, hunting through SharePoint folders for the right documents, chasing colleagues for missing inputs, and manually drafting submissions.

Ritivel deploys AI agents that transform how regulatory teams work. Our agents generate comprehensive first drafts directly in Microsoft Word, following FDA formatting requirements and pulling from your existing clinical data and prior submissions. Every data point includes citations linked back to the original source, so reviewers can verify with one click. Connected to SharePoint and Veeva, our agents automatically source the right documents. Integrated with Outlook, they handle reminder emails and follow-ups automatically.

We're engineers who previously built AI copilots at Microsoft Research. After 50+ conversations with pharma professionals, we discovered the critical bottleneck in regulatory submissions and built Ritivel to solve it.

launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We're Pavan (PK), Gunin and Nirmit – co-founders of Ritivel.

## **TL;DR**

Ritivel is an AI-native workspace for regulatory and medical writing teams at life sciences companies. Our AI agents draft CTDs, CSRs, INDs, and BLAs in minutes instead of weeks, helping drugs reach patients faster.

**Ask:** Can you introduce us to regulatory affairs leaders or CISOs at pharma companies? Contact us at [pavan@ritivel.com](mailto:pavan@ritivel.com)

<https://youtu.be/VrqJtPDy_do>

## **❌ The Problem**

Every month a drug is delayed from reaching the market costs pharma companies \~$45M in lost revenue and more importantly, delays treatment for thousands of patients who need it.

Yet regulatory teams are stuck in a painful, months-long process to create FDA submissions like CTDs, CSRs, INDs, and BLAs:

**1. Information overload** 📚 These submissions require synthesizing thousands of pages of clinical data, prior submissions, and regulatory guidance which is an overwhelming task even for experienced teams.

**2. Document hunting & version chaos** 🔄 Teams waste hours digging through SharePoint folders, juggling multiple document versions, and chasing colleagues for the right files.

**3. Endless follow-ups** 📧 Regulatory leads spend their days sending reminder emails, tracking down missing inputs, and managing status updates across teams.

**4. Manual drafting bottlenecks** ⏳ Even with all the information gathered, the first draft alone takes weeks of painstaking work by highly specialized (and expensive) regulatory writers.

---

## **🔧 Our Solution**

Ritivel deploys AI agents that transform how regulatory teams work:

**Draft the most common document types like CTDs, CSRs, INDs, and BLAs in minutes** ✍️ Our agents generate comprehensive first drafts directly in Microsoft Word, following FDA formatting requirements and pulling from your existing clinical data and prior submissions. Every data point includes citations linked back to the original source, so reviewers can verify with one click.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97327&key=user_uploads/939300/4d8b39f8-8230-4dcd-b654-c51b595d124e)

**Intelligent document retrieval** 🔗 Connected to SharePoint and Veeva, our agents automatically source the right documents from across your organization: no more digging through folders or chasing down files.

**Automated follow-ups** 📧 Integrated with Outlook, our agents handle reminder emails and follow-ups automatically, so you're not stuck chasing colleagues for missing documents.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97327&key=user_uploads/939300/aa5a53c8-8d14-4c11-a20c-fecd59724cae)

**Accelerated project management** 🚀 By automating the document gathering and drafting loop, teams can focus on review and refinement rather than administrative overhead.

\
**👬 The Team**

We're engineers who previously built AI copilots at Microsoft Research. We saw firsthand that we could create better, more specialized copilots for complex workflows.

We started by selling a generic copilot to process-heavy industries like life sciences to understand their regulatory workflows. After 50+ conversations with pharma professionals, we discovered the critical bottleneck in regulatory submissions and built Ritivel to solve it.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97327&key=user_uploads/939300/3447cd20-7180-467d-919f-e6ddb5839d7a)

## **🙏 Our Ask**

* **Know someone in pharma regulatory affairs?** We'd love an intro to regulatory affairs leaders or CISOs at pharma companies → [founders@ritivel.com](mailto:founders@ritivel.com)
* **Work at a life sciences company?** Try Ritivel and see the difference →[ ](https://www.ritivel.com/)[www.ritivel.com](http://www.ritivel.com)

Superlog is AI-native observability that's meant not to be opened. A wizard scans your repo and installs proper OpenTelemetry instrumentation, then runs daily to keep up as you ship new code. launches.body:
Hey YC! We're Nicolò and Arseniy, co-founders of Superlog ([superlog.sh](https://superlog.sh/)).

**TL;DR:** Superlog is the observability tool you're not supposed to open. A wizard scans your repo and instruments it with OpenTelemetry, and re-runs daily to keep your logs, alerts, and dashboards in sync with your code. When something breaks, an agent investigates with full context and posts one mergeable PR per incident into Slack.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AeX3pnHCMHg>

## **The Problem**

Arseniy spent years at Datadog, getting paged during the night to debug production incidents. In our first startups, we tried Sentry, Datadog, Grafana, Dash0, and nothing was good enough. 

* **Setup never ends.** Proper telemetry takes days of manual work and breaks the moment you ship new features. Half the dashboards end up empty or outdated.
* **Alert fatigue is constant.** Sentry floods Slack with duplicates and no context. The Saturday #ops ping is the worst feeling of the week.
* **The bill climbs.** Datadog invoices keep growing while engineers still spend hours configuring dashboards, chasing three AWS metrics that disagree, and copy-pasting stack traces into Claude at 11pm.

## **Our Solution**

**1. Telemetry that sets itself up.** Tell your agent:

```
Run npx skills add superloglabs/skills --all and use the skills to install Superlog in this project
```

This skill instruments your code with native OTel SDKs: proper semantic conventions, service and environment tagging. We cover all failure modes, endpoint performance, usage per tenant, and LLM/upstream cost (by callsite, tenant, and model). We run observability check-ins that keep adding logs, alerts, and dashboards as your code grows.

**2. An agent that investigates and ships PRs.** Errors get prioritised and grouped into incidents. The agent investigates with full context (logs, traces, metrics, recent deploys) and either produces a short tested PR, or posts its findings and pulls in the engineers who own the system (based on docs, prior investigations, Slack threads). One mergeable PR per incident in Slack. Merge it, ignore it, or open it as a Claude Code/Codex session and tweak.

**3. No alert fatigue.** Our custom eval setup makes sure incident summaries in your #ops channel are dense and correct, with severity and impact upfront. Every LLM-enhanced metric ships with a confidence score, so wrong guesses don't get boosted.

The telemetry you get is vendor-neutral: you keep all the OTel logs, metrics, and traces we install, even if you choose to switch providers.

## **Where We're Going**

Every engineering team in the world burns nights and weekends debugging production. We want to delete that loop. Observability should install itself, alert intelligently, and fix what it can.

## **About Us**

* **Nicolò (CEO)** — ex-BCG, math olympiad winner, scaled two startups to millions in ARR, with international enterprise contracts at Bluco (McDonald’s, Volkswagen, Dufry, etc).
* **Arseniy (CTO)** — coding since 12yo, won school olympiads, worked on high-performance data systems at Datadog and built engineering teams from scratch at Bluco.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101239&key=user_uploads/1660276/b630a0c3-d186-4f4c-95c0-6832f7893f47)

## **Our Ask**

We'd love intros to:

* Engineering leaders drowning in Sentry alerts or Datadog bills
* Startups that rolled their own observability and want to throw it away

**Try it:** [superlog.sh](https://superlog.sh/)\
**Email:** [nicolo@superlog.sh](mailto:nicolo@superlog.sh)

launches.title: Rex: Turn enterprise order-to-cash into an autonomous operation
launches.tagline: AI Operations Partner for Enterprise Order to Cash
launches.body:
Rex is an AI service that runs order-to-cash and accounts receivable operations for enterprises. Founders [Merlin Kafka](https://www.linkedin.com/in/merlinkafka/) and [Lewis Blackwood](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisblackwood) spent 4 years at an a16z-backed startup helping finance teams at startups like Cognition, Legora and Bridge automate revenue collection. The problem is 100x bigger in the enterprise, so they built Rex: agents that do the work end-to-end. Live in production with Synthesia.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BKS7qaZS8Is>

**Revenue ≠ cash**

Enterprises invoice customers, then spend months chasing the money through email chains, PDFs and ancient web portals. A $1M invoice sits unpaid because one PO number didn't match.

Multiply that across thousands of customers and you get 100+ person teams, often offshore, doing this by hand: collections, invoice submission, dispute resolution, deduction management, cash application. Order-to-cash is the most outsourced process in finance because the work needs judgment. Reading a customer's email and deciding whether their dispute is valid. Working out which of 14 open invoices a lump-sum payment covers. Knowing that this account always pays late but always pays, and that one needs escalating now.

AR automation software has existed for 20 years and the teams never got smaller, because the tools organise the work while people still do it. Businesses invoice each other tens of trillions of dollars a year; the labour and outsourcing spend on collecting it is over $100B. Until now the only way to scale was headcount or a BPO contract.

**What Rex does**

Rex connects to the ERP (NetSuite, SAP, Oracle), CRM (Salesforce), billing system and shared AR inbox, and learns how the team runs the process today. That knowledge becomes editable agent operating procedures: how to chase a Fortune 500 buyer vs a startup, which deductions get investigated vs written off, when a dispute goes to a human.

Then agents run those procedures across thousands of accounts in parallel:

* Collections and payment follow-ups, including the long tail no team gets to
* Invoice submission and status tracking inside procurement portals (SAP Ariba, Coupa, Tungsten and hundreds of others)
* Dispute and deduction investigation
* Remittance processing and cash application
* Responding to customer finance emails
* Updating ERP, CRM and billing records
* Routing exceptions to the team for approval

Portals deserve a special mention: an increasing share of enterprise invoices must be submitted and tracked inside the buyer's procurement system. It's the work AR teams hate most and the work software vendors ignore. Rex treats it as core.

**Is Rex a managed service or software?**

Enterprises can partner with Rex as a managed service provider or let their team operate Rex. AR software (dunning tools, collections worklists, AR dashboards) organises work for a team to do. Rex agents do the work, and the finance team approves exceptions. With Rex, the team stops drowning in routine chasing and handles the judgment calls. Customers compare Rex to their next AR hire, their offshore team, or their BPO contract.

**Can finance teams trust AI agents with collections?**

Autonomy is earned, not switched on. Each procedure starts supervised: Rex proposes, the team approves. Once a procedure hits its accuracy bar for the account, it graduates and runs autonomously. Safe, high-volume work goes first; judgment-heavy edges stay gated as long as the team wants. Every action is logged with its full reasoning, so finance audits the system instead of babysitting it.

**Traction**

[Rex is live in production with enterprises like Synthesia](https://www.rex.inc/customers/synthesia), running collections, portal submissions, inbox triage and cash application. Cases that used to take weeks of back and forth resolve in minutes.

**Get in touch**

If invoice volume is outgrowing the finance team, or order-to-cash runs on offshore headcount or a BPO contract, get in touch: [rex.inc](http://rex.inc)

name: Floracene
long_description:
Floracene lets any healthcare operator describe the internal tool they need and deploy it in one click - connected to production data, with read and write access scoped by the user. Think Lovable or Retool, except purpose-built for the needs of healthcare business that has no engineering team.

The bottleneck in healthcare isn't building anymore. Anyone can vibecode an 80% solution in an afternoon, custom to their own workflow, with people already on staff. The tool then dies locally on the builder’s computer, because IT (correctly) won't let anyone deploy a tool touching PHI without first-class authentication and permissioning. Our first customer had multiple employees who had each built useful tools and dashboards locally, but couldn’t actually share these with coworkers or connect to their core practice data. Within weeks of implementing Floracene, they were able to consolidate their BI tooling into Floracene and shipped 4 net-new to production.

A staggering ~$200B is spent on administrative software in healthcare every year in the US. Tens of thousands of those companies still run core operations on spreadsheets, and we're at the top of the first inning of AI adoption.

Asaph and Jonah met on the hospitals team at Palantir two years ago, and have each spent the last four years in the plumbing of US healthcare: claims, eligibility, and payor contracting. Asaph was an early PM at Garner. Jonah was a founding engineer at Metriport (YC S22) after starting his own fax-automation startup for fertility clinics.

Most real estate software stores the work. RealPact does the work.\

launches.title: Buildbox: Agent analytics for real user outcomes
launches.tagline: Find the user-facing agent failures hidden behind successful traces and evals.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** An agent can pass its evals and look healthy in traces while still failing to help users complete important tasks. Buildbox identifies those failed user journeys, ties them to business outcomes, and tests better agent behaviors and interaction patterns. Product teams get evidence-backed fixes they can review and ship.

**Ask:** If you’re building a customer-facing AI agent, we’ll help you find the agent failures you haven’t seen yet. Book 20 minutes with us:[ ](https://cal.com/marknour/20min)[cal.com/team/buildbox/discovery](http://cal.com/team/buildbox/discovery)

[www.youtube.com/watch?v=Er_CW5WS6Lw](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Er_CW5WS6Lw)

**The problem:** the most expensive agent failures rarely look like errors.

Your agent can return an answer, produce a normal-looking trace, and pass its evals while still failing to help the user. If someone has to ask the same question three times, repeatedly redirect the agent, and eventually abandon the task, was the agent actually successful?

Today, teams uncover these failures by manually reading conversations, watching sessions, checking product analytics, and comparing what they find against their most important business metrics. By the time a pattern becomes obvious, many more customers have already experienced it.

**Our solution:** Buildbox is agent analytics built around user outcomes.

Buildbox analyzes the full user journey to find where agents create friction, fail to complete a task, or leave users without the outcome they came for. It turns these breakdowns into recurring, measurable patterns, showing product teams how often they occur, who they affect, and what they cost the business in terms of activation, conversion, and retention.

For the failures that matter most, Buildbox tests better agent behaviors and interaction patterns. Teams get the underlying evidence and a validated fix they can review and ship.

If you’re shipping a new agent feature before it has real traffic, Buildbox can test it against realistic user tasks and find failure points before users encounter them.

**Who we are** 

We’re [Mark](http://www.linkedin.com/in/marknour) and [Trishala](http://www.linkedin.com/in/trishalajain7), the founders of Buildbox (YC S26). We met as undergrads at UC Berkeley and have been building together for three years. 

Before this, we worked at Netflix, Google, Amazon, and MongoDB. Across different engineering & product teams, we saw the same pattern: companies had plenty of signals & observability, but finding the issues that actually mattered and turning it into a fix still took a lot of manual detective work.

We think agents make that gap more consequential.

launches.tagline: Record how you work and turn that into agents
launches.body:
screenpipe records what you do, see and hear on your computer, makes it searchable, and gives agents the context to understand how you actually work. The project has 20K+ GitHub stars.

<https://youtu.be/c1jV6E9pyug>

Most AI agents start every task with partial context.

They can read the prompt and apps you connect. They do not remember the meeting where a decision was made, the tab you opened last Tuesday, the exact steps you took to fix a problem, or the edge case you discovered while doing the work.

screenpipe runs quietly in the background and captures screen and audio context on your machine. Then you can ask:

* maintain a second brain for every person, projects, tasks, meetings


* turn the workday into a daily recap and time breakdown for standups or client billing
* maintain a personal CRM from the people, conversations, and follow-ups seen during the day
* find commitments mentioned in meetings or messages that never made it into a task list
* analyze repeated work and produce a list of workflows worth automating
* save prompts and context from Claude, Codex, and ChatGPT into a searchable journal

Agents can use screenpipe as long-term memory, so they work from what actually happened instead of only what you remembered to paste into a prompt.

The same foundation also works across team machines. Teams can map repeated workflows, generate SOPs, find bottlenecks, and identify automation opportunities across the tools where work actually happens.

screenpipe is open source and local-first. You control what gets recorded, can exclude apps, windows, and URLs, and choose where your data lives.

I’ve been building my own AI second brain since 2020, but it could only remember what I explicitly saved. I built screenpipe so my AI could understand what I was actually doing across my screen and conversations. Other people began using it for the same reason. Today, we’re turning that foundation into context for personal and team agents.

**Our ask**

Try screenpipe and comment with the agent you would build if it could remember everything you’ve worked on.

Try screenpipe: <https://screenpipe.com>

launches.title: Alkera - The data agent that you can trust
launches.tagline: Alkera is an agent that replaces your coding agent to reliably and safely perform real data engineering/analysis/science work.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Data teams adopting AI agents want speed, but one wrong step can quietly ripple through your dbt models, dashboards, and business decisions before anyone notices. [Alkera](https://alkera.ai) **is an AI data agent for data engineers/analysts/scientists or anyone who wants to gather data insights that actually understands your data stack** (column-level lineage, graph-based planning, and a living knowledge base), so it ships data work you can trust. It's **#1 on UC Berkeley's [DataAgentBench](https://ucbepic.github.io/DataAgentBench/),** which tests complex, data-oriented tasks.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fQEVpQPYNxg>

Coding agents can write data code that runs. **For data engineering, knowing it's correct is the hard part.** This is knowing that a transformation didn't quietly redefine a column three models downstream and corrupt the revenue dashboard that the exec team checks every Monday. **For data analysis and data science, beyond data access and lineage problems, coding agents struggle with highly parallel work spread across multiple machines.** When interacting with remote computing nodes, they do so only via fragile chains of SSH commands. Long processing and training runs have you more as a babysitter than a scientist.

**Alkera is a data agent that works natively across your entire data stack, with the context and guardrails coding agents lack.** Every change it makes to a query, transformation, model, or notebook is backed by a real understanding of your pipeline.

It's **#1 on UC Berkeley's DataAgentBench,** which tests complex, data-oriented tasks. You reach it through an IDE extension (VSCode, Cursor), a CLI, or the browser — wherever you already work.

What makes it different:

* **Column-level lineage across your data stack.** Trace a single row from Snowflake, through your dbt models, to your Hex dashboard. Before the agent changes anything, it maps the _blast radius_ — every downstream table and dashboard the change would touch.
* **Graph-based planning with flexible computation.** Plan complex data tasks with parallel agents from a quick analysis to days-long modeling experiments to run across your machine and remote CPU/GPU nodes.
* **A living knowledge base.** Alkera learns your schema docs, trusted queries, and the tribal conventions that never make it into documentation — written by both agents and humans, with humans verifying what the agent adds.
* **Production protection.** Fine-grained permissions over every tool, including bash and SQL. Block a seemingly innocent SQL query with a dangerous UPDATE hidden away in a subexpression. Enforce OAuth to connect your warehouses to maintain existing data permissions.

# **Try it**

Download Alkera at <https://alkera.ai> or read the docs at <https://docs.alkera.ai>. For data engineering, point it at your stack and **watch it trace a change through your pipeline**, lighting up everything downstream. For data analysis and data science, have it **spin up parallel research agents** to explore your data. Reach out to [contact@alkera.ai](mailto:contact@alkera.ai) to see how we can tailor Alkera to your specific data apps/tools and computing environment.

# **Our team**

* Andrew Tran studied CS at Yale. At Yale, he trained LLMs to reason over multi-modal biological data. At Ramp and Hudson River Trading, he worked closely with data teams to build out ergonomic tooling for data engineers and researchers.
* Rick Gao studied CS at Yale. He was previously at Verition Fund Management, where he worked with internal data teams and counterparties to develop ingestion pipelines and internal financial models.
* Tony Li studied CS and Math at Yale. During his time at Carthage Capital and ByteDance, he worked with data engineering teams to build data pipelines, data analysis, and agentic tooling.

# **Our ask**

If you:

* perform data engineering work on production pipelines with tools like dbt and Apache Airflow
* perform data analysis/data science work in Python/R and with tools like Jupyter notebooks
* manage a data team – engineers, analysts, or scientists
* want to enable non-data experts to create data insights

Check out <https://alkera.ai> and reach out at [contact@alkera.ai](mailto:contact@alkera.ai). We’d love to showcase a demo, learn more about your data teams’ pain points, and share more about how Alkera can help supercharge them.

launches.title: Qlo - AI agents that run commercial underwriting
launches.tagline: The underwriting system of record for the AI era
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Qlo uses AI agents to run commercial underwriting operations from submission to renewal. We rebuilt the underlying system so agents can operate across the entire workflow, not sit beside another legacy system. One enterprise client signed a two-year contract, went live in May, and has since tripled weekly primary quote throughput. The end state is autonomous underwriting that follows each company’s underwriting judgment and stays within the carrier’s appetite.

Today, we’re launching the **Qlo Inbox Agent**.

<https://youtu.be/aICb20uhqhU>

### The Problem

More than $110B in commercial insurance premium flows through U.S. MGAs every year. Much of the work still begins with an email from a broker.

Commercial underwriters can spend up to 80% of their day in the inbox, chasing missing applications, loss runs, and other submission documents. Even a submission with roughly $50K in annual premium can take 48 hours to turn into a quote.

Once the information arrives, teams still need to prepare the data, run the rater, and assemble the right endorsements and quote variants.

When volume grows, teams add headcount. But underwriting judgment is hard to train and keep consistent. Costs rise, good submissions remain untouched, and inconsistent decisions can hurt loss ratios.

More premium left on the table, now with more people on payroll.

### What We Built

Qlo runs the commercial underwriting workflow from submission to renewal. Specialized agents handle each operational step, while supervisor agents coordinate the work and communicate with the underwriter.

The Inbox Agent is one of those supervisors. An underwriter can message it from a phone like a teammate. It understands the instruction, calls the right subagents, and completes the work inside Qlo.

**The underwriter makes the call. The agents make it happen.**

One of those subagents is the Rater Converter we launched on Bookface. It turns an existing rating spreadsheet into a validated digital worksheet the rest of the workflow can use.

This is what agent-compatible means to us: agents understand the workflow, have the right context, and can act across the system. Today, they execute the underwriter’s decisions. The end state is autonomous underwriting within each company’s judgment, appetite, and controls.

**The party has begun. Let the agents dance on top of Qlo.**

Guidewire and Vertafore helped define the last era of commercial insurance software. We’re building Qlo to define the next one.

### Why Us

Commercial insurance moves slowly because **distribution beats architecture**.

The system that solves the real problem will be adopted. Time will tell.

We’ll keep building.

**TLDR:** Levocred AI (YC S26) is an AI-native platform for credit funds, fintechs and banks to automate workflows like back-office tasks, portfolio monitoring, compliance and underwriting. Live across multiple credit teams, running \~$1Bn in receivables through the platform.

<https://youtu.be/OU_G096YPzo>

The winning teams will scale with token consumption, not headcount. Try it today: <https://www.levocred.ai/trynow>

**The problem**

Credit teams run on data scattered across 5-6 tools (CRM, LMS, data rooms, servicer reports) and endless spreadsheets. So highly-paid analysts become data janitors, copy-pasting between systems and rebuilding the same models — instead of the real job: underwriting and managing risk.

It's the same story across all of an analyst’s workflows (like new deals, monitoring, reporting, workouts). One example: to borrow against a credit facility (it’s like a credit card for fintechs with a limit typically in the $100Ms ), a team produces and verifies compliance certificates by hand. That's hours of Excel every time, so they draw less often than they should, leaving millions on the table.

**What is Levocred?**

Levocred is an AI employee for your credit team. It plugs into your loan tapes, credit agreements, servicer reports, and bank feeds, learns how you work, and runs the workflows your analysts do by hand today.

* Analyzes new deals and drafts the investment memos
* Monitors the portfolio, marks valuations, and answers questions in Slack ("what's our exposure to X?")
* Produces and checks compliance certificates, and handles covenant and LP reporting

Why it works when nothing else has:

* **It's AI-native, not a rules engine.** Older tools only work if you hand-code every rule, so they break on messy, real-world data. Levocred's agents read your actual documents and tapes and reason across them. We already run consumer, fintech, litigation finance, and MCA through the same engine.
* **You stay in control** with full auditability and no waiting on a vendor's engineers
* **It compounds.** Every document you load makes it smarter about your book. That data moat is yours. It’s why usage only grows.

The result: a draw that took a day of Excel takes minutes, monitoring runs continuously instead of monthly, and your team spends its time on judgment, not grunt work.
