launches.title: Avoca Systems: AI-powered radiology scheduling and communications
launches.tagline: Automating radiology scheduling and patient communications
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We’re Max Shand and Campbell Mercer, co-founders of Avoca Systems.

TL;DR: Avoca automates patient scheduling and communications for radiology groups. Our radiology-specific AI handles calls, online scheduling, faxes and e-referrals, guiding patients from referral and booking through to results and follow-up. We’re already live across more than 250 clinics, including networks operating 150+ locations.

<https://youtu.be/ZU3Ebvs5Mk0>

**What it does**

Radiology scheduling is unusually complex. A valid appointment can depend on the modality, body region, contrast requirements, patient history, preparation instructions, equipment availability, staff qualifications and referring-provider details.

These rules are fragmented across legacy systems, spreadsheets and the tacit knowledge of experienced receptionists. Generic voice and scheduling tools struggle to bring them together.

Avoca integrates with a radiology network’s existing systems and turns its workflows and operational knowledge into one automation layer:

* **AI calls:** Answers inbound calls and runs outbound campaigns for bookings, rescheduling, cancellations, preparation questions and general enquiries.
* **Online scheduling:** Lets patients upload their referral, complete the necessary clinical and safety questions, and find an appropriate appointment in real time.
* **Fax and e-referral automation:** Ingests and interprets referrals, identifies missing information and contacts patients to complete their booking.
* **Operational intelligence:** Encodes each network’s booking rules, rosters, staff capabilities, preferences and tacit knowledge so Avoca can safely fill available scanner capacity.
* **Patient communications:** Guides patients through preparation, intake, reminders, results and follow-up using voice, text and email.

**Why this matters**

Up to 30% of calls into radiology centres go unanswered as patients wait on hold. Referrals arrive through phones, websites, faxes and electronic systems, leaving staff to manually interpret documents, contact patients and coordinate appointments across multiple systems.

At the same time, radiology providers face staff shortages, rising operating costs and reimbursement pressure. Missed calls and unprocessed referrals mean patients wait longer while valuable scanner capacity goes unfilled.

Avoca helps networks capture more patient demand, reduce administrative work and complete more scans using their existing clinics, equipment and clinical systems.

**Traction**

* Partnered with 250+ clinics, including several of Australia’s largest radiology networks
* Reduced call abandonment from approximately 30% to 2%
* Patient satisfaction averaging 4.6/5
* More than 80% booking conversion for eligible patient calls in major deployments
* Integrated with leading radiology and healthcare systems, including Visage, Karisma, Comrad, Epic, Oracle Health and eClinicalWorks
* Now expanding into the United States

**Why we’re building this**

I (Max) was the first employee at Afterpay and later founded and sold Serenade. Cam was previously a principal engineer at Honey Insurance and Macquarie. Across those experiences, we saw how much better an industry can operate when complex workflows are turned into simple, intuitive products.

Healthcare is a chaotic mess of work that falls between systems: calls that go unanswered, referrals that sit in fax queues and operational knowledge that exists only in the heads of experienced staff.

We started with radiology because the scheduling complexity is exceptionally high and the consolidation of radiology clinics into large groups allowed us to focus our GTM efforts on just a few influential stakeholders who acutely feel the pain we’re solving for.

**Our big** **ask**

* Any introduction to a radiology network or health system chief executive (CEO, CIO, COO, CDO, CRO - even the new brand of CAIO - Chief AI Officer) would be hugely appreciated. We’re new to the US and eager to meet leaders tackling the patient access and scheduling challenges we’re solving.

Finally, if you operate a radiology network - or know someone who does - we’d love to hear from you. Please reply here or reach us at [hello@avocasystems.com](mailto:hello@avocasystems.com).

launches.title: hardware intelligence: AI tools for the chips your AI runs on
launches.tagline: Bringing the $20B chip tooling industry into this decade
launches.body:
---

---

**Update:** We’ve just launched our second tool, WaveZip - a genuine breakthrough method for capturing and storing waveforms. Read more at <https://hardwareintelligence.ai/wavezip/>

---

---

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KJTH-nNl6qQ>

—

We’re Athreya and Rishov - the founders of [@hardware intelligence](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/33573). We’re here to pick a fight with the $20B industry whose debuggers suck and won’t open until an ancient license server gives it permission.

**TL;DR: Our first product, Wave, is a SOTA waveform debugger that lives completely in the terminal, built for the agentic era.** An agent can jump you to the moment a design breaks, drag in waveforms and manipulate them, trace bad signals to its source and even prove its fix against the simulation - all visual. We allow teams to build better chips in less time.

**The quick ask:** If you or anyone you know builds or verifies chips (ASICs/FPGAs), please email us! We would love to talk :)

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5nXvicwWONQ>

❌ **The Problem**

The AI boom is a chip boom - more companies and teams than ever are designing silicon. However, the reality is hardware is not software: you can’t patch a chip after it ships. A bug that reaches manufacturing can be a nine-figure mistake. That’s why **companies spend 70% of the entire chip design process just on verification**.

Hardware verification engineers run thousands of simulated tests first on their code (simulation) which typically can take **hours to days**. If one of these tests fail, debugging means reading a waveform - a log of every signal, millions of ticks long, hiding the tick where a value went wrong. It’s literally a needle in a haystack… a big haystack. It’s common for these waveform files to be several gigabytes large. **Finding this needle is the single largest activity in verification.**

**The current tools are dinosaurs.** 20-year-old GUIs behind license servers whose seats run six figures a year sold by our favorite incumbents: Synopsys, Cadence, and Siemens. Free tools are even worse.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/fd100b13-f0dd-45f0-8ee4-395edf96fcae)

Yes. This is from 2026.

Software engineers got coding agents. Chip engineers got a queue for a license and whatever this is.

👋 **What Wave actually does**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/a75818b0-b001-466b-9586-705d26deb5f9)

Wave is the first of its kind! **A fully terminal-native waveform debugger with a verification agent built in.** Wave opens files before Verdi, the industry-standard viewer, finishes its license check. Let’s do a quick dive!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/ac7e5c75-8abb-4a6d-881f-a2a9b883a8b3)

**Why the terminal?** Surprisingly, most hardware engineers are terminal power users - typically doing all their coding in Vim. We wanted to meet them where they are and make our product extremely intuitive to use - we even employ Vim bindings across the interface.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/d4063fbc-2f57-4b5c-a421-bfaa697433d6)

**Ask in plain english.** _Why is a wave x at 12.4us?_ The agent will pull in signals, act on them and trace the root cause. Everything happens in front of your eyes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/8f37dd5c-22f0-4271-b665-a096c5dbfbd2)

**Pick your fix and see it.** Wave will propose different approaches with tradeoffs. The definition of “best” in hardware design depends on the use case. Maybe you want to optimize for performance? Maybe for power? Pick the one for you! Wave re-simulates and re-reads the new waveform. See a diff of how the waveform changed and a visual indication of where the fix was implemented.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/b0875bc9-fb55-4275-8c7e-11f926bc597d)

Now watch it fix a bug end to end with Rishov!

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eTycCILW6Jk>

🙏 **Asks & Offers**

If you design chips or lead a team, email us! We’d love to work with you and speed up your RTL development.

Know someone who does? Email us!

Just want to chat about hardware? **EMAIL US!!**

👬 **The Team**

We met in our freshman dorm at Georgia Tech nearly a decade ago! We became best friends and roommates for all four years of college - after, Athreya went to NYC to work at Google and Rishov stayed to do his PhD. We promised each other that once we’re free, that we’ll go all-in and work on something we’re passionate about together. Turns out, Rishov’s deep PhD thesis on chip simulation and compilers was the perfect spark.

Today we announce our company and are roommates once again ❤️

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/eef30a82-c606-494a-a093-3649920c7857)

—

Say hi 👋 [hi@hardwareintelligence.ai](mailto:hi@hardwareintelligence.ai) · [hardwareintelligence.ai](http://hardwareintelligence.ai)

[@Athreya Anand](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/551607) · [athreya@hardwareintelligence.ai](mailto:athreya@hardwareintelligence.ai)

[@Rishov Sarkar](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2565323) · [rishov@hardwareintelligence.ai](mailto:rishov@hardwareintelligence.ai)

P.S. Wave is just the start 👀 We got some super cool things coming to close the loop of hardware engineering.

Hey everyone. You’ve might of heard of Open AI, Open Router, OpenCode, OpenWork….

Introducing [OpenTag](https://www.tryopentag.com/?utm_source=yc&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=yc-launch&utm_content=launch-page) - the model agnostic Claude Tag.

We started early access a 2 weeks ago and are live with 10 teams.

If you've seen Claude Tag, you know the interface: tag an AI in Slack, hand it a task, get the result in the thread. We think that's the right interface. We built OpenTag because we think the multiplayer harness should be model agnostic. When a better model ships, your coworker gets better the same day, benefiting from the performance and cost improvements.

OpenTag is an AI coworker that lives inside of Slack. You invite it into the channels you want. It picks up how the company runs, how decisions are made, who owns what. It helps the team coordinate and builds automations for workflows that it sees as repetitive. It asks for tools and visibility the way an A-player hire does, and it tries to grow its own scope and agency. It starts as an intern and tries to earn the COO job. As it works, it writes a company wiki of how you actually run. That wiki compounds as a company brain, so OpenTag only gets sharper with time. Throw it anything. It does its best, and it asks for help when it’s blocked. The result lands in the thread, with sources, where the whole team can see it.

**Four parts, one coworker:**

1. **Ambient and proactive agents -** properly sandboxed with its own computer and browser, so you can trust them with actual tasks instead of babysitting chat windows.
2. **A wiki that maintains itself —** no more stale handbooks. OpenTag writes down how the company actually runs and keeps it current. Teammates can read it. Agents can read it.
3. **Automations that suggest themselves -** OpenTag watches how your team works and surfaces the repetitive stuff worth automating, so you're not designing workflows from a blank page.
4. **Built for multiplayer** - OpenTag is designed with proper permissioning that matches how your team operates.

**2 minutes to start.** Add OpenTag to Slack, invite it to the channels where work happens, give it a job. It’ll ask for the tools it needs (whatever the job touches). It only reads the channels you invited it to.

**Built by software engineers who’ve shipped products used by millions.**

The three of us worked together at Lilac Labs (YC S24) and all went to Berkeley. Tony (CEO) was software at Tesla and Intel. Shelden (CTO) was at Flatiron Health, Roche, and Certik (cyber security). Engineers don't have time to continually improve the agents they've shipped — the context bloat, overly chatty subagents, and broken tool calls sit in production traces nobody reads, quietly hurting agent efficiency. With Papaya they connect their agent directly via SDK, get actionable recommendations on how to improve quality, latency, and cost, and the ones they approve are pushed to production as pull requests.

launches.title: Papaya - Continuous Optimization for your AI agents
launches.tagline: Papaya finds what's hurting your agent's quality, cost, and latency, and fixes it for you.
launches.body:
Hey everyone! 👋 \
\
We're Macy, Faiz and Niyaz - co-founders of[ Papaya](https://papaya.fyi) 

**TL;DR**

Papaya is the optimization engine for AI agents. Connect your production agent and Papaya watches every action, finds what's hurting quality, cost, and latency, and gives you the fix. Once a fix is in place, Papaya makes sure your agent doesn't regress. Teams running Papaya are seeing 20%+ improvements to quality, latency, and cost.

**Ask:** If you run an agent in production, connect it to Papaya. Grab a time to get started [here](https://cal.com/macy-mody/macy-papaya).

<https://youtu.be/cG9iIVB5Psk>

**The Problem**

We’ve been building agentic systems for years (6 years to be exact…before it was cool), including really large ones that helped run major workflows inside Amazon. We know firsthand that the hard part isn’t getting an agent to work, it’s keeping it working at a high quality bar. We consistently saw that every model update and every prompt change shifted behavior in ways nobody caught until something downstream looked wrong. The only way to find out what changed was to pull traces and read them by hand.

Most companies shipping agents today are focused on the next feature for customers and they don't have time to fully maintain what's already been released. When we built our own agent as a three-person team, we hit the same wall. We needed to make sure our agent had high quality answers, was fast for our customers, and as low cost as possible, but we had to look at everything by hand. Every hour we spent examining traces was an hour we couldn’t spend on new product development. That's why we built Papaya.

**How Papaya works 🔧** 

At Papaya, our goal is to do the hard AI engineering work for you, staying up to date on the latest and greatest research so you can take advantage of this knowledge through optimizations. Simply stream your production traces through a lightweight SDK. From there, Papaya:

* **Finds your use cases**: groups every run by the job the agent is doing, so you're looking at "refund requests," not "run 4812."
* **Runs 200+ analyses**: checks every use case against 200+ research-backed failure patterns across quality, cost, and latency.
* **Ranks the fixes by impact**: every recommendation comes with an estimated effect on quality, latency, and cost. Approve the ones you want directly in Papaya and Papaya opens the PR.
* **Watches for regression**: once a fix ships, Papaya keeps checking that the improvement holds.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=115486&key=user_uploads/2135001/0a49f356-ac11-44d5-bcc1-69caf4ba64d9)


**Our Ask 🙏**

* Run an agent in production? Connect it to Papaya. Grab a time with us [here](https://cal.com/macy-mody/macy-papaya).
* Know any companies spending tons of time maintaining and fixing their agents? Intro us at [macy@papaya.fyi](mailto:macy@papaya.fyi).
* Building agents and want a second set of eyes? Ping us. We are happy to help however we can!

**The Team**

We've spent over 10 years building large scale agentic systems at Amazon, and we've scaled other YC startups from $0 to $10M ARR through acquisition. We started out building an analytics agent. The harness we built to optimize our own agent became the center of every prospect conversation, so we pivoted to it. Meet our team below :)
